changes.reason: Turn off freezing by projectability, so that frozen states come only from the energy window (at most 10, under num_wann = 12). This keeps the frozen window at E_F + 2.02 eV, which contains the Fermi level, and keeps the s + d projector set that removed the diffuse p2 functions.

diagnosis: Attempt 1 dropped the diffuse Ti p2 pseudo-atomic orbital, keeping s2 + d1. That cut the count from 18 to 12 functions (2 atoms × (1+5)). Wannier90 then refused to start because, at some k-point, more than 12 states were frozen. The refusal is not caused by the energy window: below dis_froz_max = E_F + 2.02 eV there are at most 10 states (frozen_capacity), which fits, and the window could go as high as E_F + 6.6 eV. The extra frozen states come from the projectability criterion. With dis_proj_max = 0.95, Ti-d states above E_F + 2 eV that the s + d orbitals describe well (p ≥ 0.95) are also frozen, and these push the count past 12. Dropping p2 was itself a sound move: in attempt 0 the 18-function model failed even without truncation (η2 = 56.7 meV untruncated, 114.6 meV truncated). Its functions were broad, 7–10 Å² each, centred 0.6–0.8 Å off the atoms. Six of them together carry about 0.77 of the hopping weight beyond r_c, and the error sits right at E_F (DFT bands 12 and 14, errors up to 0.8 eV). So I keep s + d and fix the side of the inequality that actually overflowed: I turn off freezing by projectability. That leaves the energy window, which contains E_F, as the only thing that freezes states.
